title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 86 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 482–484 (Night 86, continuing directly from nights-85), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 86 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The old woman takes the five slave-girls and Ṣafiyya away with a sealed cup for the king to drink; he is found dead, and a paper in the cup tells that Dhāt al-Dawāhī has carried Ṣafiyya off to Constantinople and means war. Dandān finishes his account to Ḍawʾ al-Makān, who weeps, is steadied by the chamberlain, and takes up the throne, reviewing the troops and the treasuries, until dawn cuts Shahrazād off. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّادِسَةُ وَالثَّمَانُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sādisatu wa-al-thamānūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the sixth and the eighty,
sentences.i: And when it was the eighty-sixth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ قَالَ لِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ إِنَّ أَبَاكَ قَالَ لِلْعَجُوزِ لَمَّا طَلَبَتْ مِنْهُ الْجَوَارِيَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna al-wazīra dandāna qāla li-ḍawʾi al-makāni inna abāka qāla li-al-ʿajūzi lammā ṭalabat minhu al-jawāriya
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the vizier Dandān said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān: Truly your father said to the old-woman, when she asked of him the slave-girls:
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the vizier Dandān said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān: “Your father said to the old woman, when she asked him for the slave-girls:
sentences.n: The print has قات, a misprint for قالت, corrected here. It also runs أن into the word before it (السعيدان, “the happy — that”); it is read as two words.

sentences.t: إِنَّ عِنْدِى جَارِيَةً رُومِيَّةً اسْمُهَا صَفِيَّةُ وَرُزِقْتُ مِنْهَا بِوَلَدَيْنِ أُنْثَى وَذَكَرٍ وَلَكِنَّهُمَا فُقِدَا مِنْ مُنْذُ سِنِينَ
sentences.tr: inna ʿindī jāriyatan rūmiyyatan ismuhā ṣafiyyatu wa-ruziqtu minhā bi-waladayni unthā wa-dhakarin wa-lākinnahumā fuqidā min mundhu sinīna
sentences.l: ‘Truly with me is a slave-girl, a Rūmī, her name Ṣafiyya, and I was provided by her with two children, a female and a male, but the two of them were lost from since years;
sentences.i: ‘I have a Rūmī slave-girl named Ṣafiyya, and I had two children by her, a girl and a boy, but they have been lost these many years.
sentences.n: من منذ doubles the preposition (min, “from,” and mundhu, “since”); it is kept as printed, as in the night before.

sentences.t: فَخُذِيهَا مَعَكِ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ تَحْصُلَ لَهَا الْبَرَكَةُ وَلَعَلَّ رِجَالَ الْغَيْبِ أَنْ يَدْعُوا اللَّهَ لَهَا بِأَنْ يَرُدَّ عَلَيْهَا وَلَدَيْهَا وَيَجْمَعَ شَمْلَهَا بِهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-khudhīhā maʿaki li-ajli an taḥṣula lahā al-barakatu wa-laʿalla rijāla al-ghaybi an yadʿū allāha lahā bi-an yaradda ʿalayhā waladayhā wa-yajmaʿa shamlahā bihimā
sentences.l: so take her with you, for the sake that the blessing may come about for her; and perhaps the men of the unseen will call upon God for her, that He return to her her two children and gather her scattered-union with them.’
sentences.i: So take her with you, that she may receive the blessing; perhaps the Men of the Unseen will pray to God for her, that He give her back her two children and reunite her with them.’
sentences.n: لَعَلَّ followed by أَنْ and a plural verb (يدعوا), as the print has it. شمل, “union, gathered state,” is what scatters when a family is parted: “to gather someone’s shaml” is to reunite them.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْعَجُوزُ نِعْمَ مَا قُلْتَ وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ أَعْظَمَ غَرَضِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-ʿajūzu niʿma mā qulta wa-kāna dhālika aʿẓama gharaḍihā
sentences.l: And the old-woman said: Excellent is what you said; and that was the greatest of her aim.
sentences.i: The old woman said, “Well said!” and this was the very thing she most wanted.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ وَالِدَكَ أَخَذَ فِي تَمَامِ صِيَامِهِ فَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا وَلَدِي إِنِّي مُتَوَجِّهَةٌ إِلَى رِجَالِ الْغَيْبِ فَأَحْضِرْلِي صَفِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna wālidaka akhadha fī tamāmi ṣiyāmihi fa-qālat lahu yā waladī innī mutawajjihatun ilā rijāli al-ghaybi fa-aḥḍirlī ṣafiyyata
sentences.l: Then truly your father took to the completion of his fast, and she said to him: O my child, I am one-turning to the men of the unseen, so make-present to me Ṣafiyya.
sentences.i: Then your father went on to the end of his fast, and she said to him, “My son, I am about to set out for the Men of the Unseen, so bring me Ṣafiyya.”
sentences.n: فاحضرلي is written as one word in the print, as is common.

sentences.t: فَدَعَابِهَا فَحَضَرَتْ فِي سَاعَتِهَا فَسَلَّمَهَا إِلَى الْعَجُوزِ فَخَلَطَتْهَا بِالْجَوَارِي
sentences.tr: fa-daʿā bihā fa-ḥaḍarat fī sāʿatihā fa-sallamahā ilā al-ʿajūzi fa-khalaṭathā bi-al-jawārī
sentences.l: So he called for her, and she came-present in her hour, and he handed her to the old-woman, and she mixed her with the slave-girls.
sentences.i: He sent for her, and she came at once; he handed her over to the old woman, who mixed her in among the slave-girls.
sentences.n: دعا بـ means “send for, call for” (the بِـ is the one the verb takes). في ساعتها, “in her hour,” is “on the spot.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلَتِ الْعَجُوزُ مَخْدَعَهَا وَخَرَجَتْ لِلسُّلْطَانِ بِكَأْسٍ مَخْتُومٍ وَنَاوَلَتْهُ لَهُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma dakhalati al-ʿajūzu makhdaʿahā wa-kharajat li-al-sulṭāni bi-kaʾsin makhtūmin wa-nāwalat-hu lahu wa-qālat lahu
sentences.l: Then the old-woman entered her private-chamber and went out to the sultan with a cup, sealed, and handed it to him, and said to him:
sentences.i: Then the old woman went into her chamber and came out to the sultan with a sealed cup. She handed it to him and said,
sentences.n: كأس is treated as masculine here (مختوم), which the word allows.

sentences.t: إِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ الثُّلَٰثِينَ فَادْخُلِ الْحَمَّامَ ثُمَّ اخْرُجْ مِنْهُ وَادْخُلْ خَلْوَةً مِنَ الْخَلَاوَى الَّتِي فِي قَصْرِكَ
sentences.tr: idhā kāna yawmu al-thulāthīna fa-udkhuli al-ḥammāma thumma ukhruj minhu wa-udkhul khalwatan mina al-khalāwā allatī fī qaṣrika
sentences.l: When it is the day of the thirty, then enter the bath, then go out from it, and enter a retreat, from the retreats which are in your palace,
sentences.i: “When the thirtieth day comes, go into the bath, then come out of it and enter one of the private rooms in your palace,
sentences.n: الثلثين is the print’s spelling of الثلاثين; the dagger alif marks the long vowel the print leaves out. خلوة is a room for being alone.

sentences.t: وَاشْرَبْ هَذَا الْكَأْسَ وَنَمْ فَقَدْ نِلْتَ مَا تَطْلُبُ وَالسَّلَامُ مِنِّي عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-ishrab hādhā al-kaʾsa wa-nam fa-qad nilta mā taṭlubu wa-al-salāmu minnī ʿalayka
sentences.l: and drink this cup, and sleep; for you have attained what you seek, and peace from me be upon you.”
sentences.i: and drink this cup and sleep, for you will have what you seek. Peace from me be upon you.”

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ فَرِحَ الْمَلِكُ وَشَكَرَهَا وَقَبَّلَ يَدَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika fariḥa al-maliku wa-shakarahā wa-qabbala yadayhā
sentences.l: And at that the king rejoiced, and thanked her, and kissed her two hands.
sentences.i: At that the king was glad; he thanked her and kissed her hands.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ اسْتَوْدَعْتُكَ اللَّهَ فَقَالَ لَهَا وَمَتَى أَرَاكِ أَيَّتُهَا السَّيِّدَةُ الصَّالِحَةُ فَإِنِّي أَوَدُّ أَنْ لَا أُفَارِقَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu istawdaʿtuka allāha fa-qāla lahā wa-matā arāki ayyatuhā al-sayyidatu al-ṣāliḥatu fa-innī awaddu an lā ufāriqaki
sentences.l: And she said to him: I deposit you with God. And he said to her: And when shall I see you, O lady, the righteous? For I wish not to part from you.
sentences.i: She said to him, “I leave you in God’s keeping,” and he said, “When shall I see you again, O righteous lady? I would not be parted from you.”
sentences.n: اودّ is printed with its shadda.

sentences.t: فَدَعَتْ لَهُ وَتَوَجَّهَتْ وَمَعَهَا الْجَوَارِي وَالْمَلِكَةُ صَفِيَّةُ وَقَعَدَ الْمَلِكُ بَعْدَهَا ثَلَٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ
sentences.tr: fa-daʿat lahu wa-tawajjahat wa-maʿahā al-jawārī wa-al-malikatu ṣafiyyatu wa-qaʿada al-maliku baʿdahā thalāthata ayyāmin
sentences.l: So she prayed for him, and set out, and with her the slave-girls and the queen Ṣafiyya; and the king sat after her three days.
sentences.i: She prayed for him and set out, with the slave-girls and Queen Ṣafiyya in her train, and the king waited three days after her departure.
sentences.n: ثلثة is the print’s spelling of ثلاثة (dagger alif).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ هَلَّ الشَّهْرُ فَقَامَ الْمَلِكُ وَدَخَلَ الْحَمَّامَ وَخَرَجَ مِنَ الْحَمَّامِ وَدَخَلَ الْخَلْوَةَ الَّتِي فِى الْقَصْرِ وَأَمَرَأَنْ لَايَدْخُلَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ وَرَدَّ الْبَابَ عَلَيْهِ،
sentences.tr: thumma halla al-shahru fa-qāma al-maliku wa-dakhala al-ḥammāma wa-kharaja mina al-ḥammāmi wa-dakhala al-khalwata allatī fī al-qaṣri wa-amara an lā yadkhula ʿalayhi aḥadun wa-radda al-bāba ʿalayhi
sentences.l: Then the new-moon appeared, and the king arose, and entered the bath, and went out from the bath, and entered the retreat which is in the palace, and commanded that none enter upon him, and shut the door upon him,
sentences.i: Then the new moon showed, and the king rose, went into the bath and came out of it, entered the private room in the palace, ordered that no one come in to him, and shut the door.
sentences.n: هل الشهر, “the month appeared,” is said of the new crescent coming into sight. أمر أن (amara an) is written run together in the print (وامران).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ شَرِبَ الْكَأْسَ وَنَامَ وَنَحْنُ قَاعِدُونَ فِي انْتِظَارِهِ إِلَى آخِرِ النَّهَارِ
sentences.tr: thumma shariba al-kaʾsa wa-nāma wa-naḥnu qāʿidūna fī intiẓārihi ilā ākhiri al-nahāri
sentences.l: then he drank the cup and slept; and we were sitting in waiting for him until the end of the day.
sentences.i: Then he drank the cup and fell asleep, while we sat waiting for him until the end of the day.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَخْرُجْ مِنَ الْخَلْوَةِ فَقُلْنَا لَعَلَّهُ تَعْبَانُ مِنَ الْحَمَّامِ وَمِنْ سَهَرِ اللَّيْلِ وَصِيَامِ النَّهَارِ فَبِسَبَبِ ذَلِكَ نَامَ فَانْتَظَرْنَاهُ ثَانِيَ يَوْمٍ فَلَمْ يَخْرُجْ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yakhruj mina al-khalwati fa-qulnā laʿallahu taʿbānu mina al-ḥammāmi wa-min sahari al-layli wa-ṣiyāmi al-nahāri fa-bi-sababi dhālika nāma fa-intaẓarnāhu thāniya yawmin fa-lam yakhruj
sentences.l: And he did not come out of the retreat, so we said: Perhaps he is tired from the bath, and from the night’s wakefulness, and the day’s fasting, so by reason of that he slept. And we waited for him a second day, and he did not come out.
sentences.i: He did not come out of the room. We said, “Perhaps he is worn out from the bath, the sleepless nights and the fasting days, and that is why he is sleeping.” We waited for him a second day, and still he did not come out.
sentences.n: فبسبب ذلك: the بِـ in بِسَبَبِ means “by reason of.” تعبان is a Middle Arabic form (“tired”).

sentences.t: فَوَقَفْنَا بِبَابِ الْخَلْوَةِ وَأَعْلَنَّا بِرَفْعِ الصَّوْتِ لَعَلَّهُ يَنْتَبِهُ وَيَسْأَلُ عَنِ الْخَبَرِ
sentences.tr: fa-waqafnā bi-bābi al-khalwati wa-aʿlannā bi-rafʿi al-ṣawti laʿallahu yantabihu wa-yasʾalu ʿani al-khabari
sentences.l: So we stood at the door of the retreat, and we announced with the raising of the voice, in the hope that he would wake and ask about the news.
sentences.i: So we stood at the door of the room and called out aloud, hoping he would wake and ask what was happening.
sentences.n: أعلنّا is أعلننا with the two nūns joined by a shadda. وقف بـ means “stand at.”

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَحْصُلْ مِنْهُ ذَلِكَ فَخَلَعْنَا الْبَابَ وَدَخَلْنَا عَلَيْهِ فَوَجَدْنَاهُ قَدْ تَمَزَّقَ وَهَرَّأَ لَحْمُهُ وَتَفَتَّتَ عَظْمُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yaḥṣul minhu dhālika fa-khalaʿnā al-bāba wa-dakhalnā ʿalayhi fa-wajadnāhu qad tamazzaqa wa-harraʾa laḥmuhu wa-tafattata ʿaẓmuhu
sentences.l: But that did not come about from him, so we tore-off the door and entered upon him, and found him torn apart, and his flesh in tatters, and his bone crumbled.
sentences.i: He gave no sign, so we broke down the door and went in to him. We found him torn to pieces, his flesh in shreds and his bones crumbled.
sentences.n: هرّأ is kept as printed, with its shadda and hamza; it is the verb “to tatter, reduce to rags” used of flesh, here read as an intransitive “fell into shreds.”

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَيْنَاهُ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْحَالَةِ عَظُمَ عَلَيْنَا ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾaynāhu ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥālati ʿaẓuma ʿalaynā dhālika
sentences.l: And when we saw him in this state, that became great upon us.
sentences.i: When we saw him in that state, we were overwhelmed.

sentences.t: وَأَخَذْنَا الْكَأْسَ فَوَجَدْنَا فِي غِطَائِهِ قِطْعَةَ وَرَقٍ مَكْتُوبًا فِيهَا مَنْ أَسَاءَ لَابِسْتَوْحِشَ مِنْهُ وَهَذَا جَزَاءُ مَنْ يَتَحَيَّلُ عَلَى بَنَاتِ الْمُلُوكِ وَيُفْسِدُهُنَّ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadhnā al-kaʾsa fa-wajadnā fī ghiṭāʾihi qiṭʿata waraqin maktūban fīhā man asāʾa lābistawḥisha minhu wa-hādhā jazāʾu man yataḥayyalu ʿalā banāti al-mulūki wa-yufsiduhunna
sentences.l: And we took the cup, and found in its lid a piece of paper, written-upon in it: Whoever did evil [...] from it; and this is the recompense of whoever schemes against the daughters of kings and corrupts them.
sentences.i: We took up the cup and found in its lid a slip of paper, and written on it: “Whoever does wrong [...] And this is the reward of one who schemes against the daughters of kings and corrupts them.
sentences.n: The print has لابستوحش, kept as printed because the reading is doubtful: it may be a misprint for لا يستوحش, “does not feel alarmed,” but the clause then still lacks its sense, so the English leaves the words after “does wrong” unrendered rather than guess.

sentences.t: وَالَّذِي نُعَلِّمُ بِهِ كُلَّ مَنْ وَقَفَ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْوَرَقَةِ أَنَّ شَرْكَانَ لَمَّا جَاءَ إِلَى بِلَادِنَا قَدْ أَفْسَدَ عَلَيْنَا الْمَلِكَةَ أَبْرِيزَ وَمَاكَفَاهُ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى أَخَذَهَا مِنْ عِنْدِنَا وَجَاءَ بِهَا إِلَيْكُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-alladhī nuʿallimu bihi kulla man waqafa ʿalā hādhihi al-waraqati anna sharkāna lammā jāʾa ilā bilādinā qad afsada ʿalaynā al-malikata abrīza wa-mākafāhu dhālika ḥattā akhadhahā min ʿindinā wa-jāʾa bihā ilaykum
sentences.l: And that which we inform by it every one who stood upon this paper is that Sharkān, when he came to our lands, had corrupted for us the queen Abrīz, and that was not enough for him until he took her from with us and came with her to you.
sentences.i: What we make known by it to everyone who comes upon this paper is that Sharkān, when he came to our country, corrupted our queen Abrīz, and that was not enough for him: he took her from us and brought her to you.
sentences.n: وقف على means “come upon, learn of.” جاء بـ means “bring.” The charge against Sharkān is false: it is the old woman’s own scheme.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَهَا مَعَ عَبْدٍ أَسْوَدَ فَقَتَلَهَا وَوَجَدْنَاهَا مَقْتُولَةً فِى الْخَلَاءِ مَطْرُوحَةً عَلَى الْأَرْضِ
sentences.tr: thumma arsalahā maʿa ʿabdin aswada fa-qatalahā wa-wajadnāhā maqtūlatan fī al-khalāʾi maṭrūḥatan ʿalā al-arḍi
sentences.l: Then he sent her with a black slave, and he killed her, and we found her killed in the open-country, thrown upon the ground.
sentences.i: Then he sent her off with a black slave, who killed her; we found her dead in the open country, flung on the ground.
sentences.n: The paper’s story is the old woman’s own invention: she is the one who has Ṣafiyya.

sentences.t: فَهَذَا مَا هُوَ فِعْلُ الْمُلُوكِ وَمَا جَزَاءُ مَنْ يَفْعَلُ هَذَا الْفِعْلَ إِلَّا مَاحَلَّ بِهِ وَأَنْتُمْ لَاتَتَّهِمُوا أَحَدًا بِقَتْلِهِ فَمَا قَتَلَهُ إِلَّا الْعَاهِرَةُ الشَّاطِرَةُ الَّتِي اسْمُهَا ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي
sentences.tr: fa-hādhā mā huwa fiʿlu al-mulūki wa-mā jazāʾu man yafʿalu hādhā al-fiʿla illā mā ḥalla bihi wa-antum lā tattahimū aḥadan bi-qatlihi fa-mā qatalahu illā al-ʿāhiratu al-shāṭiratu allatī ismuhā dhātu al-dawāhī
sentences.l: So this is not the deed of kings, and the recompense of one who does this deed is nothing but what befell him; and you, do not accuse anyone of his killing, for none killed him but the whore, the cunning, whose name is Dhāt al-Dawāhī.
sentences.i: This is no act worthy of kings, and one who does such a thing gets only what has befallen him. Do not accuse anyone of killing him: it was the cunning whore called Dhāt al-Dawāhī who killed him.
sentences.n: ما هو فعل الملوك: the ما is a negative, “this is not the deed of kings.” ذات الدواهي, “mistress of calamities,” is the old woman’s true name. The print runs ما حل together (ماحلّ) and sets لا تتهموا as one word.

sentences.t: وَهَا أَنَا أَخَذْتُ زَوْجَةَ الْمَلِكِ صَفِيَّةَ وَمَضَيْتُ بِهَا إِلَى وَالِدِهَا أَفْرِيدُونَ مَلِكِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-hā anā akhadhtu zawjata al-maliki ṣafiyyata wa-maḍaytu bihā ilā wālidihā afrīdūna maliki al-quṣṭanṭīniyyati
sentences.l: And here am I: I have taken the king’s wife, Ṣafiyya, and gone with her to her father Afrīdūn, king of Constantinople,
sentences.i: Here I am: I have taken the king’s wife Ṣafiyya and I am going with her to her father Afrīdūn, king of Constantinople,

sentences.t: وَلَا بُدَّأَنْ نَغْزُوَكُمْ وَنَقْتُلَكُمْ وَنَأْخُذَ مِنْكُمُ الدِّيَارَ فَتَهْلِكُونَ عَنْ آخِرِكُمْ وَلَا يَبْقَى مِنْكُمْ دَيَّارٌ وَلَا مَنْ يَنْفُخُ النَّارَ إِلَّا مَنْ يَعْبُدُ الصَّلِيبَ وَالزُّنَّارَ
sentences.tr: wa-lā budda an naghzuwakum wa-naqtulakum wa-naʾkhudha minkumu al-diyāra fa-tahlikūna ʿan ākhirikum wa-lā yabqā minkum dayyārun wa-lā man yanfukhu al-nāra illā man yaʿbudu al-ṣalība wa-al-zunnāra
sentences.l: and it is not avoidable that we raid you, and kill you, and take from you the abodes, so you will perish to your last, and there will remain of you no dweller, nor one who blows the fire, except whoever worships the cross and the belt.
sentences.i: and we shall surely march on you, kill you and take your lands, and you will perish to the last man; not a soul will be left of you, not so much as one to blow on a fire, save those who worship the cross and wear the girdle.”
sentences.n: ولا بد أن is written ولا بدان. ما يبقى منكم ديّار ولا من ينفخ النار, “no dweller and no one to blow the fire,” is a proverbial way to say that nobody at all remains. الزنار is the belt that marked Christians under Muslim rule.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرَأْنَا هَذِهِ الْوَرَقَةَ عَلِمْنَا أَنَّ الْعَجُوزَ خَدَعَتْنَا وَتَمَّتْ حِيلَتُهَا عَلَيْنَا فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ صَرَخْنَا وَلَطَمْنَا عَلَى وُجُوهِنَا وَبَكَيْنَا فَلَمْ يَفِدْنَا الْبُكَاءُ شَيْأً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qaraʾnā hādhihi al-waraqata ʿalimnā anna al-ʿajūza khadaʿatnā wa-tammat ḥīlatuhā ʿalaynā fa-ʿinda dhālika ṣarakhnā wa-laṭamnā ʿalā wujūhinā wa-bakaynā fa-lam yafidnā al-bukāʾu shayʾan
sentences.l: And when we read this paper, we knew that the old-woman had deceived us, and her stratagem had been completed upon us; and at that we cried out, and struck upon our faces, and wept, and the weeping did not avail us anything.
sentences.i: When we read the paper we knew that the old woman had tricked us and her plot had succeeded against us. We cried out and struck our faces and wept, but weeping did us no good.
sentences.n: The print has يقدنا, a misprint for يفدنا (the ف and ق differ by a dot), corrected here.

sentences.t: وَاخْتَلَفَتِ الْعَسَاكِرُ فِيمَنْ يَجْعَلُونَهُ سُلْطَانًا عَلَيْهِمْ فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُكَ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ أَخَاكَ شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-ikhtalafati al-ʿasākiru fī-man yajʿalūnahu sulṭānan ʿalayhim fa-minhum man yurīduka wa-minhum man yurīdu akhāka sharkāna
sentences.l: And the armies differed about whom they would make sultan over them, and among them are those who want you, and among them those who want your brother Sharkān.
sentences.i: The armies disagreed about whom to make sultan over them: some wanted you, and some wanted your brother Sharkān.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ نَزَلْ فِي هَذَا الِاخْتِلَافِ مُدَّةَ شَهْرٍ ثُمَّ جَمَعَنَا بَعْضُنَا وَأَرَدْنَا أَنْ نَمْضِىَ إِلَى أَخِيكَ شَرْكَانَ فَسَافَرْنَا إِلَى أَنْ وَجَدْنَاكَ وَهَذَا سَبَبُ مَوْتِ السُّلْطَانِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam nazal fī hādhā al-ikhtilāfi muddata shahrin thumma jamaʿanā baʿḍunā wa-aradnā an namḍiya ilā akhīka sharkāna fa-sāfarnā ilā an wajadnāka wa-hādhā sababu mawti al-sulṭāni ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni
sentences.l: And we did not cease in this disagreement a period of a month; then some of us gathered others of us, and we wished to go to your brother Sharkān, and we travelled until we found you; and this is the cause of the death of the sultan ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.i: We stayed in this dispute for a month; then we gathered together and meant to go to your brother Sharkān, and we travelled until we found you. That is how Sultan ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān died.”

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ مِنْ كَلَامِهِ بَكَيٰ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ هُوَ وَأُخْتُهُ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ وَبَكَى الْحَاجِبُ أَيْضًا ثُمَّ قَالَ الْحَاجِبُ لِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha al-wazīru dandānu min kalāmihi bakā ḍawʾu al-makāni huwa wa-ukhtuhu nuzhatu al-zamāni wa-bakā al-ḥājibu ayḍan thumma qāla al-ḥājibu li-ḍawʾi al-makāni
sentences.l: And when the vizier Dandān finished his speech, Ḍawʾ al-Makān wept, he and his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān, and the chamberlain wept also; then the chamberlain said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān:
sentences.i: When the vizier Dandān had finished speaking, Ḍawʾ al-Makān wept, he and his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān, and the chamberlain wept too. Then the chamberlain said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān,
sentences.n: بكي is the print’s spelling of بكى (the dagger alif marks the long vowel).

sentences.t: أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ إِنَّ الْبُكَاءَ لَايُفِيدُكَ شَيْأً وَلَايَنِيدُكَ إِلَّا أَنَّكَ تَشُدُّ قَلْبَكَ وَتُقَوِّي عَزْمَكَ وَتُؤَيِّدُ مَمْلَكَتَكَ وَمَنْ خَلَّفَ مِثْلَكَ مَا مَاتَ
sentences.tr: ayyuhā al-maliku inna al-bukāʾa lā yufīduka shayʾan wa-lā yanīduka illā annaka tashuddu qalbaka wa-tuqawwī ʿazmaka wa-tuʾayyidu mamlakataka wa-man khallafa mithlaka mā māta
sentences.l: O king, truly weeping does not avail you anything, nor [...] you, except that you brace your heart, and strengthen your resolve, and support your kingdom; and whoever left behind one like you has not died.
sentences.i: “O king, weeping will do you no good, nor [...]; what you must do is steady your heart, strengthen your resolve and uphold your kingdom. He who leaves a son like you has not died.”
sentences.n: ولاينيدك is kept as printed; the verb ينيد is not one I can identify, and the sense is probably “nor help you,” so the word is left unrendered here rather than guessed.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ سَكَتَ عَنْ بُكَائِهِ وَأَمَرَ بِنَصْبِ السَّرِيرِ خَارِجَ الدِّهْلِيزِ ثُمَّ أَمَرَأَنْ يَعْرِضُوا عَلَيْهِ الْعَسَاكِرَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika sakata ʿan bukāʾihi wa-amara bi-naṣbi al-sarīri khārija al-dihlīzi thumma amara an yaʿriḍū ʿalayhi al-ʿasākira
sentences.l: And at that he fell silent from his weeping, and commanded the setting-up of the throne outside the entrance-hall; then he commanded that they present to him the armies.
sentences.i: At that he stopped weeping and ordered the throne set up outside the entrance hall; then he ordered the troops to be paraded before him.

sentences.t: وَوَقَفَ الْحَاجِبُ بِجَانِبِهِ وَجَمِيعُ السِّلَحْدَارِيَّةِ مِنْ وَرَائِهِ وَوَقَفَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ قُدَّامَهُ وَوَقَفَ كُلُّوَاحِدٍ مِنَ الْأُمَرَاءِ وَأَرْبَابِ الدَّوْلَةِ فِي مَرْتَبَتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-waqafa al-ḥājibu bi-jānibihi wa-jamīʿu al-silaḥdāriyyati min warāʾihi wa-waqafa al-wazīru dandānu quddāmahu wa-waqafa kullawāḥidin mina al-umarāʾi wa-arbābi al-dawlati fī martabatihi
sentences.l: And the chamberlain stood at his side, and all the armour-bearers behind him, and the vizier Dandān stood before him, and each one of the emirs and the lords of the state stood in his rank.
sentences.i: The chamberlain stood at his side with all the armour-bearers behind him, the vizier Dandān stood in front of him, and each of the emirs and officers of state stood in his proper rank.
sentences.n: كلواحد is written as one word in the print. السلحدارية, from the Turkish silāḥdār, are the weapon-bearers of the guard.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ قَالَ لِلْمُوزْبِرْدَنْدَانَ أَخْبِرْنِي بِخَزَائِنِ أَبِي فَقَالَ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً وَأَخْبَرَهُ بِخَزَائِنِ الْأَمْوَالِ وَبِمَا فِيهَا مِنَ الذَّخَائِرِ وَالْجَوَاهِرِ وَعَرَضَ عَلَيْهِ مَا فِي خِزْنَتِهِ مِنَ الْأَمْوَالِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika ḍawʾa al-makāni qāla li-al-mūzbirdandāna akhbirnī bi-khazāʾini abī fa-qāla samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan wa-akhbarahu bi-khazāʾini al-amwāli wa-bi-mā fīhā mina al-dhakhāʾiri wa-al-jawāhiri wa-ʿaraḍa ʿalayhi mā fī khiznatihi mina al-amwāli
sentences.l: Then the king Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to al-mūzbirdandān: Inform me of the treasuries of my father. And he said: Hearing and obedience. And he informed him of the treasuries of the monies, and of what is in them of the stores and the jewels, and presented to him what was in his treasury of the monies.
sentences.i: Then King Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to the vizier Dandān, “Tell me about my father’s treasuries.” He said, “With hearing and obedience,” and told him of the treasure-houses and what they held of stores and jewels, and showed him the money in his own treasury.
sentences.n: The print has للموزبردندان, a garbled form of للوزير دندان, “to the vizier Dandān”; the garble is kept as printed, because the correction is a guess about several letters, and the English reads it as the vizier. خزنته is kept as printed; it may be خزانته with a dropped alif.

sentences.t: فَأَنْفَقَ عَلَى الْعَسَاكِرِ وَخَلَعَ عَلَى الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ خِلْعَةً سَنِيَّةً وَقَالَ لَهُ أَنْتَ فِي مَكَانِكَ فَقَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَدَعَا لَهُ بِالْبَقَاءِ ثُمَّ خَلَعَ عَلَى الْأُمَرَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-anfaqa ʿalā al-ʿasākiri wa-khalaʿa ʿalā al-wazīri dandāna khilʿatan saniyyatan wa-qāla lahu anta fī makānika fa-qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-daʿā lahu bi-al-baqāʾi thumma khalaʿa ʿalā al-umarāʾi
sentences.l: So he spent upon the armies, and bestowed upon the vizier Dandān a robe of honour, lofty, and said to him: You are in your place. And he kissed the ground between his two hands, and called down on him continuance; then he bestowed robes upon the emirs.
sentences.i: He paid out money to the troops and gave the vizier Dandān a splendid robe of honour, saying, “You stay in your post.” Dandān kissed the ground before him and prayed for his long life; then the king gave robes of honour to the emirs.
sentences.n: خلع على, “bestow a robe upon,” is the usual way a ruler honours an officer. أنت في مكانك confirms the vizier in his office.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ قَالَ لِلْحَاجِبِ اعْرِضْ عَلَىَّ الَّذِي مَعَكَ مِنْ خَرَاجِ دِمَشْقَ فَعَرَضَ عَلَيْهِ صَنَادِيقَ الْمَالِ وَالتُّحَفَ وَالْجَوَاهِرَ فَأَخَذَهَا وَفَرَّقَهَا عَلَى الْعَسَاكِرِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu qāla li-al-ḥājibi uʿriḍ ʿalayya alladhī maʿaka min kharāji dimashqa fa-ʿaraḍa ʿalayhi ṣanādīqa al-māli wa-al-tuḥafa wa-al-jawāhira fa-akhadhahā wa-farraqahā ʿalā al-ʿasākiri
sentences.l: Then he said to the chamberlain: Present to me what is with you of the tribute of Damascus. And he presented to him chests of money and rarities and jewels, and he took them and distributed them upon the armies.
sentences.i: Then he said to the chamberlain, “Show me what you have brought of Damascus’s tribute.” The chamberlain showed him chests of money, rare objects and jewels, and he took them and shared them out among the troops.
sentences.n: The print has على, which the sense reads as عليّ, “to me,” after the imperative: not “upon the one who…”.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, with its rhyme on -āḥ, as in every night.
